title: observability: token-level metrics + tracing + dashboards + alert tuning
author: Aisha Patel
description: Add token-level metrics and tracing integration for cost/latency breakdowns; ship Grafana dashboards and tuned alert rules to reduce noise. Motivation: customers and SRE teams need per-token cost visibility and traceable request->model spans to diagnose tail-latency and KV cache behavior. This PR implements the metrics surface at the runtime boundary, plumbs tracing contexts for per-token spans, adds a set of Grafana dashboards for token cost/latency and KV cache hit/miss rates, and updates alert thresholds to reduce duplicate incidents while keeping SLO coverage. Changes include: new token_metrics exporter, lightweight per-token tracing spans, dashboard panels for token cost and latency percentiles, alert rule tuning informed by 30d traffic percentiles, and docs. The description below lists the primary changes, testing notes, and rollout plan. Testing: unit tests for metric cardinality and integration test that validates tracing spans and dashboard panels render expected series; load test with synthetic traffic to validate alert thresholds. Rollout: feature gated by obs.token_level.enabled which defaults to off in staging; gradual rollout to 10% of traffic for 48h before turning on for all regions. Follow-ups: propagate token cost to billing pipeline (ENG-4100) and extend support for additional model backends.

release_notes: Added token-level cost and latency metrics, tracing spans for token generation and KV cache access, Grafana dashboards for token cost/latency and KV cache metrics, and tuned alerts to reduce noise. Feature is feature-gated and will be rolled out gradually.
notes_on_deployment: Feature gated by obs.token_level.enabled; default off in staging and can be enabled per-cluster via charts/observability/values.yaml. Rollout plan: 10% traffic for 48h -> 50% for 72h -> global. Monitoring during rollout: P95 token generation latency and token_cost per-request must remain within baseline.
